newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso soft but mkt calm as Brazil woes fade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso soft but mkt calm as Brazil woes fade.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened marginally weaker on Wednesday due to dealers covering short dollar positions carried over from the prior session amid a market calmed by a recovery in Brazilian equity markets and a strong U.S. long bond, dealers said.
"Some still had some (dollar) shorts to cover from yesterday," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart opened trade 0.8 and 0.5 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9275/7.9330 and 7.9230/7.9270 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile begun the session 4.3 centavos weaker at 7.9180/7.9230 per dollar, after lining up with late weakness in other contracts on Tuesday.
The Bovespa index of leading shares traded in Sao Paulo was up 2.63 percent to 11,922 after posting a sharp fall on Tuesday that triggered a speculative run on the peso.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 17/32 to yield 6.51 percent in the wake of mild consumer price data released in early trade.
Dealers predicted the 48-hour peso could trade in a range of 7.9100/7.9600 per dollar. (( --Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
